sources.name: React Bits

license.name: MIT + Commons Clause
license.redistribution_note: Application use is allowed by current terms, but redistribution of the components/library is restricted; inspect current LICENSE.md before reuse.

inspected_artifacts.finding: PixelSwap bounds generated windows with MAX_PIXELS, maps nine reveal-order patterns, computes easing/keyframes, supports hover/click/manual control, and exposes interruption/state hooks; the reusable mechanism is bounded content-window reveal, not the demo styling.
The demo is a context artifact for composition and controls; it must be read with the component source rather than treated as implementation truth.
React Bits publishes copy-install registry payloads in multiple technology variants, so adaptation must account for the selected distribution variant and its local dependency/style boundary.
The repository declares 165+ animated components and four implementation variants plus creative tools; README is discovery scope only, not sufficient evidence for adopting a specific effect.

when_to_use: Creative animated React components or effects where product fit justifies them.
when_not_to_use: Do not redistribute React Bits components as a competing component library; do not use it as sole accessibility semantics authority.

inspected_artifacts.finding: The React renderer composes iconNode geometry with context-controlled size/color/stroke, preserves absolute stroke width, and defaults unlabeled icons to aria-hidden while respecting explicit accessibility props.
Tests explicitly verify aria-hidden defaults, explicit aria overrides, title/children accessibility behavior and snapshot rendering, so icon adoption must preserve these semantic conditions.
Icon generation is centralized rather than hand-authored per consumer, supporting family consistency and a stable semantic component boundary.
Framework delivery is a package-level concern; importing icons should preserve tree-shaking/delivery conventions rather than copying arbitrary SVG fragments without provenance.

when_to_use: Use when icon-system evidence fits the concrete UI decision.
when_not_to_use: Do not authorize material transfer until the v6 role-specific dossier is complete.
